nations.name: Paiwan
nations.lands: Southern Central Mountain Range across Pingtung and Taitung counties, Taiwan

facts.text: About 102,730 Paiwan people were counted in January 2020, living in the southern mountains of Pingtung and Taitung.
The Ravar branch of the Paiwan is known for outstanding carving and pottery.

nations.name: Wanniyala-Aetto
nations.lands: Eastern Sri Lanka, including the Maduru Oya area

facts.text: In 1983, 51,468 hectares of Wanniyala-Aetto customary land were declared the Maduru Oya National Park.
Their own name, Wanniyala-Aetto, means forest dwellers, and their ancestors lived on the island long before the Sinhalese and the Tamils arrived.

nations.name: Tsou
nations.lands: Alishan Township in Chiayi County, plus Nantou and Kaohsiung, Taiwan

facts.text: The Tsou homeland centres on Alishan Township in Chiayi County, southwest of Yushan in central Taiwan.
The Tsou population was 6,702 in January 2020.

nations.name: Mentawai
nations.lands: The Mentawai Islands, including Siberut, off West Sumatra, Indonesia

facts.text: On Siberut, a UNESCO biosphere reserve since 1981, Mentawai communities use the forest with care, guided by traditional knowledge.

source.title: Siberut Biosphere Reserve, Indonesia
source.publisher: UNESCO Man and the Biosphere Programme

facts.text: Siberut, home to many Mentawai communities, is the largest of the four Mentawai Islands west of Sumatra.

source.title: Siberut Biosphere Reserve, Indonesia
source.publisher: UNESCO Man and the Biosphere Programme

nations.name: Lumad
nations.lands: Mindanao, Philippines

facts.text: Lumad is a shared name for many Indigenous peoples of Mindanao, among them the Manobo, Subanon, Mandaya, Talandig and Teduray.
Lumad advocacy, with allies, helped write two important provisions into the 1987 Philippine Constitution.

nations.name: Khasi
nations.lands: Khasi Hills of Meghalaya, India, and nearby Bangladesh

facts.text: The Khasi Hills Autonomous District Council has a wing that oversees the Elakas, the traditional Khasi states.

source.title: General Administration Department and Elaka Administration

facts.text: Apart from Shillong's municipality and cantonment, all of Meghalaya is governed under the Sixth Schedule, the only northeast state where this is so.

nations.name: Bunun
nations.lands: Both sides of the Central Mountain Range in Nantou, Hualien, Taitung and Kaohsiung, Taiwan

facts.text: The Bunun live higher in the mountains than any other Indigenous people in Taiwan, mostly between 500 and 1,500 metres.
About 59,536 Bunun people were counted in January 2020, with homes in Nantou, Hualien, Taitung and Kaohsiung.

nations.name: Tamang
nations.lands: Hills around the Kathmandu Valley and central Nepal

facts.text: The Tamang are on the Nepal government's official list of Adivasi Janajati, or Indigenous nationalities.

source.title: Adivasi Janajati list
source.publisher: National Foundation for Development of Indigenous Nationalities, Nepal

facts.text: Tamang is the mother tongue of about 4.88 percent of Nepal's population, according to the 2021 census.

nations.name: Akha
nations.lands: Northern Thailand, eastern Myanmar and northern Laos

facts.text: The Akha are one of more than 20 highland Indigenous peoples of northern Thailand.

nations.name: Saisiyat
nations.lands: Hsinchu and Miaoli counties in northwestern Taiwan

facts.text: The Saisiyat live in northwestern Taiwan, in Hsinchu County and Miaoli County on either side of Ngangihaw mountain.
The Saisiyat population was 6,730 in January 2020.

nations.name: Truku
nations.lands: Xiulin, Wanrong and Zhuoxi townships in Hualien County, Taiwan

facts.text: The Truku were officially recognized as one of Taiwan's Indigenous peoples in 2004.
About 32,333 Truku people were counted in January 2020, mostly in Hualien County.

nations.name: Sediq
nations.lands: Mountain areas of Nantou and Hualien in central Taiwan

facts.text: Three subgroups make up the Sediq, each with its own group identity: Seediq Tgdaya, Sediq Toda and Sejiq Truku.
About 10,452 Sediq people were counted in January 2020, mostly in the mountains of Nantou and Hualien.

nations.name: Bhil
nations.lands: Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Rajasthan and Maharashtra, India

facts.text: India's government names the Bhil among the tribal peoples whose movements strengthened the country's freedom struggle.

source.title: Cabinet approves declaration of 15th November as Janjatiya Gaurav Divas
source.publisher: Prime Minister's Office, Government of India

nations.name: Marma
nations.lands: Chittagong Hill Tracts of Bangladesh

facts.text: Together, the Chakma, Marma and Tripura make up about 90 percent of the Indigenous peoples of the Chittagong Hill Tracts.

nations.name: Yakthung
nations.lands: Limbuwan in the eastern hills of Nepal, including Taplejung, Panchthar, Terhathum and Ilam, plus Jhapa, Morang and Sunsari, with communities in Sikkim and Darjeeling, India

facts.text: In Nepal's 2021 census, 84.5 percent of Yakthung people reported Limbu as their mother tongue, a language with its own script, Sirijanga.

source.title: लिम्बु (Limbu)
source.publisher: National Foundation for Development of Indigenous Nationalities, Nepal

facts.text: In 2021 Nepal's Language Commission recommended Limbu, alongside Maithili, as an official language of Province 1 in eastern Nepal.

source.title: Language Commission recommends province-wise official languages before government

nations.name: Tharu
nations.lands: The Terai plains of southern Nepal, and neighbouring India

facts.text: The Tharu are on the Nepal government's official list of Adivasi Janajati, or Indigenous nationalities.

source.title: Adivasi Janajati list
source.publisher: National Foundation for Development of Indigenous Nationalities, Nepal

facts.text: Tharu is the mother tongue of about 5.88 percent of Nepal's population, according to the 2021 census.

nations.name: Kurukh
nations.lands: Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh and West Bengal in India, with communities in Assam, Bangladesh and Nepal

facts.text: Odisha counted 358,112 Kurukh (Oraon) people in 2011; many farm and practice crafts such as carpentry, rope making and weaving date palm leaf mats.

source.title: Odisha State Tribal Museum: Oraon
source.publisher: Odisha State Tribal Museum (SCSTRTI, Government of Odisha)

facts.text: Twelve to thirty Kurukh villages join in a Parha council, where members of each village council meet under a Parha chief.

source.title: Oraon
source.publisher: Dr. Ramdayal Munda Tribal Welfare Research Institute, Jharkhand

nations.name: Thao
nations.lands: Ita Thao Village by Sun Moon Lake and Dapinglin, Nantou County, Taiwan

facts.text: Thao people live mainly in Ita Thao Village in Yuchi Township and in Dapinglin, Shuili Township, both in Nantou County. They numbered about 817 in January 2020.
Thao oral history tells of ancestors who followed a white deer to Sun Moon Lake and found a fertile place full of fish.

nations.name: Pinuyumayan
nations.lands: Taitung City and Beinan Township on the Taitung Plain, Taiwan

facts.text: Taitung City and Beinan Township on the Taitung Plain are the heart of Pinuyumayan life today.
About 14,517 Pinuyumayan people were counted in January 2020, and many have moved from eastern Taiwan to cities, where they are active in many fields.

nations.name: Santal
nations.lands: Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha and nearby states of India, northwest Bangladesh, and Nepal

facts.text: On 25 December 2025, India's Constitution was released in the Santali language, written in the Ol Chiki script.

source.title: President of India releases the Constitution of India in the Santhali language

facts.text: Odisha counted 894,764 Santal people in the 2011 census, most living in settled villages of 50 to 100 households.

source.title: Odisha State Tribal Museum: Santal
source.publisher: Odisha State Tribal Museum (SCSTRTI, Government of Odisha)

nations.name: Munda
nations.lands: Jharkhand, Odisha, West Bengal, Chhattisgarh and Bihar in India, with communities in Bangladesh

facts.text: Mundari has its own script, known in the community as Mundari Bani; a version reformed in 2008 by Munda community bodies is in the Unicode Standard.

source.title: Chapter 13, South and Central Asia-II (The Unicode Standard, Version 18.0)

facts.text: Munda call their dance durang and their song susun, and both women and men dance at social events and seasonal festivals.

source.title: Munda
source.publisher: Dr. Ramdayal Munda Tribal Welfare Research Institute, Jharkhand

nations.name: Ho
nations.lands: Kolhan region of Jharkhand and northern Odisha, with communities in West Bengal and Bihar, India

facts.text: In Odisha, Ho farmers grow paddy, maize and ragi, tend kitchen gardens, and gather mushrooms, mahua and greens from the forest.

source.title: Odisha State Tribal Museum: Ho
source.publisher: Odisha State Tribal Museum (SCSTRTI, Government of Odisha)

facts.text: The Ho language has its own recently devised alphabet, Warang Citi, which is encoded in the Unicode Standard and used by a yearly and a biweekly publication.

source.title: Chapter 13, South and Central Asia-II (The Unicode Standard, Version 18.0)

nations.name: Kanakanavu
nations.lands: Namaxia District, Kaohsiung City, Taiwan

facts.text: On June 26, 2014, Taiwan's government recognized the Kanakanavu as an independent people, the 16th on the official list.
Some Kanakanavu people understand their name as people living in a forest of Taiwan giant bamboo.

nations.name: Rai
nations.lands: Majh Kirat, also called Khambuwan, in the middle hills of eastern Nepal between the Dudh Koshi and Arun rivers, plus Jhapa, Morang, Sunsari and the Kathmandu Valley

facts.text: The Kirat Rai Yayokkha, founded in 1990, works to unite Nepal's diverse Rai communities and to promote Rai languages, arts and literature.
The Rai are a multilingual people: the Kirat Rai Yayokkha has registered 26 Rai language groups, among them Bantawa, Chamling and Kulung.

source.title: राई (Rai)
source.publisher: National Foundation for Development of Indigenous Nationalities, Nepal

nations.name: Rukai
nations.lands: Southern Central Mountain Range in Kaohsiung, Pingtung and Taitung, Taiwan

facts.text: About 13,465 Rukai people were counted in January 2020, living in Kaohsiung, Pingtung and Taitung.
For the Rukai, the lily stands for purity and courage, and the right to wear lily ornaments sits at the heart of their culture.

nations.name: Gond
nations.lands: Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Telangana, Odisha and neighboring states of central India

facts.text: Masaram Gondi, a script created in 1918 by Munshi Mangal Singh Masaram of Madhya Pradesh to write the Gondi language, is still used today in handwritten and printed materials.

source.title: Chapter 13, South and Central Asia-II (The Unicode Standard, Version 18.0)

facts.text: Gond painting, mostly made in Patangarh village in Dindori district, gained worldwide recognition after shows in Tokyo and Paris and became a livelihood for many tribal families.

source.title: Gond Art: Details about Gond Tribal Art and Painting of India

nations.name: Dayak
nations.lands: Borneo: Kalimantan (Indonesia), Sabah and Sarawak (Malaysia) and Brunei

facts.text: Dayak is a shared name for many Indigenous peoples of Borneo, by some estimates about 450 ethnolinguistic groups.
Dayak peoples share traditions of longhouse living and customary law known as adat.

nations.name: Wurundjeri Woi Wurrung
nations.lands: Melbourne and surrounding lands, including the Birrarung (Yarra River), Victoria, Australia

facts.text: The Wurundjeri council was set up in 1985 by Wurundjeri descendants and gained Registered Aboriginal Party status for cultural heritage in 2008.

source.title: Recent Past & Present
source.publisher: Wurundjeri Woi Wurrung Cultural Heritage Aboriginal Corporation

facts.text: In 2017 a Yarra River protection bill was the first legislation put before Victoria's parliament with a dual Aboriginal language title: Wilip-gin Birrarung murron, keep the Birrarung alive.

source.title: Recent Past & Present
source.publisher: Wurundjeri Woi Wurrung Cultural Heritage Aboriginal Corporation

nations.name: iTaukei
nations.lands: Fiji

facts.text: The iTaukei Land Trust Board, set up in 1940, manages iTaukei land for its owners, whether a yavusa, mataqali or tokatoka.
The iTaukei Affairs Board, set up in 1944 as the Fijian Affairs Board, is the main advisory and coordinating body for iTaukei affairs, supporting village, tikina and provincial leaders.

nations.name: Kosraeans
nations.lands: Kosrae, an island state in the east of the Federated States of Micronesia, with the municipalities of Lelu, Malem, Tafunsak and Utwe

facts.text: Kosrae State has its own constitutional government, with a legislature elected by voters in the districts of Lelu, Malem, Tafunsak and Utwe.

source.title: Kosrae
source.publisher: Legal Information System of the Federated States of Micronesia

facts.text: In 2017 Kosraean elders proposed protecting Kosrae's mountain range, seen as the figure Mahkontowe, now the Mahkontowe Conservation Area under Kosrae State law.

nations.name: Gunditjmara
nations.lands: South-west Victoria, including Budj Bim and Tae Rak (Lake Condah), Australia

facts.text: Gunditj Mirring Traditional Owners Aboriginal Corporation was set up in 2005 to continue Gunditjmara connection to country, including native title work.

source.title: Gunditj Mirring Traditional Owners Aboriginal Corporation | GMTOAC | 248 Condah Estate Road, Heywood VIC, Australia
source.publisher: Gunditj Mirring Traditional Owners Aboriginal Corporation

facts.text: All of the Budj Bim Cultural Landscape is Aboriginal owned or managed.

source.title: World heritage conservation of Budj Bim

nations.name: Te Arawa
nations.lands: Rotorua and the Rotorua lakes district, Bay of Plenty, Aotearoa New Zealand

facts.text: Rotorua was declared New Zealand's first bilingual district in 2017, and the council has since worked with Te Tatau o Te Arawa on changes like bilingual road signs.
The Te Arawa Lakes settlement, signed in 2004, provided for title to 13 lakebeds to be returned to Te Arawa, a large confederation of iwi and hapū.

source.title: Te Arawa Lakes
source.publisher: Te Kāhui Whakatau (Treaty Settlements), New Zealand Government

nations.name: Yapese
nations.lands: the main islands of Yap (Yap, Gagil, Tomil and Rumung) in Yap State, Federated States of Micronesia

facts.text: Yap's state constitution creates the Council of Pilung and the Council of Tamol, councils of traditional leaders whose work concerns tradition and custom.

source.title: Yap State Code, Title 5: Traditional Leaders and Traditions
source.publisher: Legal Information System of the Federated States of Micronesia

facts.text: Under Yap State law the two councils advise the Governor and Legislature and work to promote and preserve the traditions and customs of the people.

source.title: Yap State Code, Title 5: Traditional Leaders and Traditions
source.publisher: Legal Information System of the Federated States of Micronesia

nations.name: Tuvaluans
nations.lands: the nine islands of Tuvalu in the central Pacific, including Funafuti

facts.text: Each island in Tuvalu has a falekaupule, a traditional assembly of elders also called te sina o fenua, the grey-hairs of the land.

source.title: The Local Government System in Tuvalu

facts.text: Tuvaluan has eight dialects from eight of the islands, and the name Tuvalu joins tu, to stand, with valu, eight.

source.title: Tuvalu language activity book
source.publisher: Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa

nations.name: Arrernte
nations.lands: Alice Springs and surrounding lands in Central Australia, Northern Territory, Australia

facts.text: Lhere Artepe Aboriginal Corporation, their native title body, looks after five Indigenous Land Use Agreements plus a land release agreement.

source.title: About Us | Lhere Artepe Aboriginal Corporation

facts.text: Arrernte people from three estate groups, Antulye, Irlpme and Mparntwe, are the traditional owners of Alice Springs and its surrounding land.

source.title: About Us | Lhere Artepe Aboriginal Corporation

nations.name: Tongans
nations.lands: the Kingdom of Tonga in the South Pacific, including Tongatapu, Vava'u, Ha'apai, 'Eua and the Niuas

facts.text: Tonga's 2021 census counted 100,179 people in the kingdom, a young population with a median age of 19 for males and 22 for females.
Lakalaka, often called Tonga's national dance, joins choreography, oratory and sung polyphony, and is performed at coronations and constitution anniversaries.

source.title: Lakalaka, dances and sung speeches of Tonga

nations.name: Tiwi
nations.lands: The Tiwi Islands (Bathurst and Melville Islands), about 80 km north of Darwin in the Arafura Sea, Northern Territory, Australia

facts.text: There are eight landowning groups on the Tiwi Islands, and Tiwi people have an unbroken history of occupying and owning their islands.
The Tiwi Islands, about 80 km north of Darwin, are home to just over 3,000 people, more than 90 percent of them Tiwi.

nations.name: Gamilaraay
nations.lands: North-central New South Wales into southern Queensland, Australia

facts.text: The Australian National University teaches Gamilaraay as a heritage language that its custodians are actively reviving.

source.title: Gamilaraay - Introduction to an Australian Indigenous Language

facts.text: Student work in the ANU Gamilaraay course feeds into materials for Gamilaraay and Yuwaalaraay language revival, taught with a free textbook called Wiidhaa.

source.title: Gamilaraay - Introduction to an Australian Indigenous Language

nations.name: Ngāti Porou
nations.lands: Te Tairāwhiti, the East Coast of the North Island, from Pōtikirua to Te Toka-a-Taiau, Aotearoa New Zealand

facts.text: Ngāti Porou's tribal area runs down Te Tairāwhiti, between Pōtikirua (Lottin Point) in the north and Te Toka-a-Taiau in the south.
The Ngāti Porou pepeha names Hikurangi as their mountain and Waiapu as their river.

nations.name: ni-Vanuatu
nations.lands: the islands of the Republic of Vanuatu in the south-west Pacific, including Malakula and the central and northern islands

facts.text: Vanuatu Cultural Centre fieldworkers, or filwokas, are volunteers nominated by their communities across the islands to promote, protect and preserve kastom.

source.title: Grassroots Badly Burnt: the loss of ni-Vanuatu archaeologists whose careers spanned 50 years

facts.text: In 1998 Na'hai speakers of south Malakula opened the Na'hai Kaljaral Senta, the first language-based cultural centre in Vanuatu.

source.title: Kastom as Development: Opening the Na'hai Kaljaral Senta

nations.name: Meriam
nations.lands: Mer (Murray Island) and nearby islands in the eastern Torres Strait, Queensland, Australia

facts.text: Meriam Mir is the traditional language of Mer, an island in the far east of the Torres Strait from which the Great Barrier Reef can be seen.

source.title: Murray Island - Mer Eruer Uteb
source.publisher: Tagai State College (Queensland Department of Education)

nations.name: Rotumans
nations.lands: the island of Rotuma and its islets, about 500 km north of Fiji's main islands, and communities across Fiji

facts.text: Rotuma is divided into seven districts, each led by a district chief, the gagaj 'es itu'u, with village groups called ho'aga under their own chiefs.

source.title: Hierarchy (Kato'aga: Rotuman Ceremonies)
source.publisher: The Rotuma Website, University of Hawai'i

facts.text: Rotumans are a distinct people with their own language, Fäeag Rotuạm, which New Zealand celebrates each year in Rotuman Language Week.

source.title: Gasav Ne Fäeag Rotuạm Ta: Rotuman Language Week

nations.name: Kanak
nations.lands: New Caledonia, including Grande Terre and the Loyalty Islands

facts.text: Since 2016 every pupil in New Caledonia must be taught the fundamentals of Kanak culture, and every school must offer teaching in Kanak languages.

source.title: Organisation coutumière kanak
source.publisher: Institut de la statistique et des études économiques Nouvelle-Calédonie (ISEE)

facts.text: Kanak society is organised by custom: clans join into tribes within customary districts, which are grouped into eight customary areas.

source.title: Organisation coutumière kanak
source.publisher: Institut de la statistique et des études économiques Nouvelle-Calédonie (ISEE)

nations.name: Ngāi Tūhoe
nations.lands: Te Urewera, in the eastern North Island, Aotearoa New Zealand

facts.text: A Treaty settlement signed in 2013 provided for Te Urewera, the Tūhoe homeland, to have its own law and a separate legal identity, governed by Tūhoe and Crown nominees.

source.title: Ngāi Tūhoe
source.publisher: Te Kāhui Whakatau (Treaty Settlements), New Zealand Government

facts.text: Tūhoe had about 9,300 registered members at the time of their 2013 Treaty settlement.

source.title: Ngāi Tūhoe
source.publisher: Te Kāhui Whakatau (Treaty Settlements), New Zealand Government

nations.name: Tokelauans
nations.lands: the three atolls of Tokelau, Atafu, Nukunonu and Fakaofo, in the South Pacific

facts.text: In Tokelau the Taupulega, the village councils of elders, remain the ultimate source of authority, and they grant the General Fono its powers.
The role of Ulu-o-Tokelau, head of the national government, rotates each year among the elected leaders of Tokelau's three atolls.

nations.name: I-Kiribati
nations.lands: the Republic of Kiribati in the central Pacific, across the Gilbert, Phoenix and Line Islands

facts.text: In Kiribati the mwaneaba, the traditional meeting house, is where village decisions are made by the unimwane, the senior men, whose seating shows their standing.

source.title: Te Mwaneaba ni Kiribati: The Traditional Meeting House of Kiribati
source.publisher: Shima: The International Journal of Research into Island Cultures

facts.text: In 2010 the Phoenix Islands Protected Area, about 408,250 square kilometres of ocean and islands, became the first World Heritage site in Kiribati.

nations.name: Wiradjuri
nations.lands: Central New South Wales, the country of the Wambool (Macquarie), Kalari (Lachlan) and Murrumbidjeri (Murrumbidgee) rivers, Australia

facts.text: A Charles Sturt University course shaped by Wiradjuri Elders works to build a living community of Wiradjuri speakers; it won a 2019 MacJannet Prize.

source.title: The Graduate Certificate in Wiradjuri Language Culture and Heritage, Charles Sturt University (Australia)
source.publisher: Talloires Network of Engaged Universities (Tufts University)

facts.text: Wiradjuri country covers a large part of New South Wales, reaching out from the Great Dividing Range.

nations.name: Papuan peoples
nations.lands: The Papua region of Indonesia, the western half of the island of New Guinea

facts.text: Men and women in Papua use the noken to carry garden produce, and it may also be worn at festivities or given as a peace offering.

source.title: Noken multifunctional knotted or woven bag, handcraft of the people of Papua

facts.text: The noken, a bag that communities in Papua knot or weave by hand from wood fibre or leaves, was inscribed on a UNESCO list for urgent safeguarding in 2012.

source.title: Noken multifunctional knotted or woven bag, handcraft of the people of Papua

nations.name: Mā'ohi
nations.lands: French Polynesia, including Tahiti and the other islands of its five archipelagos

facts.text: A new website interface announced in 2017 by the Tahitian Academy, Fare Vāna'a, adds French to Tahitian search to its Tahitian to French dictionary.

source.title: Evolution du site internet du Fare Vāna’a & application
source.publisher: Service public de la Polynésie française (DGEN)

facts.text: UNESCO honours mā'ohi skill in sailing outrigger canoes across long stretches of ocean, navigating by observing natural phenomena.

nations.name: Seminole Nation of Oklahoma
also: The Great Seminole Nation of Oklahoma
nations.lands: Wewoka and Seminole County, Oklahoma, United States; earlier homelands in Florida

facts.text: The Seminole Nation of Oklahoma is made up of fourteen bands, and its General Council seats two representatives from each band rather than from districts.

source.title: The Great Seminole Nation of Oklahoma: Written Testimony to the Senate Committee on Indian Affairs
source.publisher: Seminole Nation of Oklahoma, via U.S. Senate Committee on Indian Affairs

facts.text: The Seminole Nation Language Program works to maintain, revitalize and carry forward the language and traditional ways of the Seminole people.

nations.name: Rappahannock Indian Tribe
nations.lands: the lower Rappahannock and Mattaponi river watersheds in Virginia, as described by the Tribe's environmental department

facts.text: The Tribe's environmental department says it coordinates the Return to the River youth program.

source.title: Department Of Environmental Services | Rappahannock Indian Tribe

facts.text: The Tribe dates its incorporation to 1921 as part of efforts to strengthen its government and seek recognition.

nations.name: United Cherokee AniYunWiYa Nation
nations.lands: Guntersville, Alabama

facts.text: A January 2020 post describes a Word of the Month practice series, with a new calendar of practice planned for February.
In January 2020, the Nation announced a plan to highlight enrolled citizens' crafted items in its public posts.

source.title: Attention: United Cherokee AniYunWiYa Nation Artisans - UCAN

nations.name: Saint Regis Mohawk Tribe
nations.lands: Akwesasne, on the St. Lawrence River in northern New York, United States; the wider Akwesasne community extends into Canada

facts.text: The Saint Regis Mohawk Tribal Council is made up of three Chiefs, three Sub-Chiefs and a Tribal Clerk, with elections scheduled each year and set terms of office.

source.title: History of Tribal Government | SRMT - NSN

facts.text: The Tribe describes its original homeland as northeastern New York State, reaching into southern Canada and Vermont.

source.title: History of Tribal Government | SRMT - NSN

nations.name: Coharie Tribe
nations.lands: Harnett and Sampson Counties in southeastern North Carolina, where the Tribe locates its present community

facts.text: The Tribe's government page describes the Coharie Intra-Tribal Council as representing Harnett and Sampson Counties.
The Tribe's history locates the present Coharie population in North Carolina's Harnett and Sampson Counties.

nations.name: Seneca Nation
nations.lands: Allegany, Cattaraugus and Oil Spring territories in Western New York, United States

facts.text: The Seneca Nation governs itself under a constitution established in 1848, with a 16-member Tribal Council drawn equally from the Cattaraugus and Allegany territories.

source.title: Seneca Nation of Indians - Official Website

facts.text: The Seneca Nation runs a language immersion program so students can hold conversations in Onöndowa’ga:’ Gawë:nö’, the Seneca language, alongside classes and online learning.

nations.name: Cherokee Nation
nations.lands: Tahlequah and a 14-county reservation area in Oklahoma, United States; original homelands in the Southeast

facts.text: Cherokee Nation governs through legislative, executive and judicial branches and serves people across a 14-county reservation area.
Written Cherokee uses a syllabary, not an alphabet, with 85 distinct characters; Cherokee Nation teaches it through an immersion school and a master-apprentice program.

nations.name: Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians
nations.lands: The Qualla Boundary in western North Carolina, United States, beside the Great Smoky Mountains

facts.text: As a sovereign nation, the Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians makes its own laws, holds its own elections and runs its own government and institutions.

source.title: Home - Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians

facts.text: The Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians makes its home on the 56,000-acre Qualla Boundary, next to Great Smoky Mountains National Park.

source.title: NC Tribal Communities | NC DOA
source.publisher: North Carolina Department of Administration, Commission of Indian Affairs

nations.name: Seminole Tribe of Florida
nations.lands: Big Cypress, Brighton, Fort Pierce, Hollywood, Immokalee and Tampa reservations in Florida, United States

facts.text: The Tribal Council, with a Chairman, a Vice-Chairman and representatives from each reservation, is the chief governing body of the Seminole Tribe of Florida.
Adding the Tampa and Immokalee reservations brought the Seminole Tribe of Florida's federal trust lands to more than 90,000 acres.

nations.name: Southeastern Mvskoke Nation
nations.lands: Near Troy in Alabama; its history describes organization around Pike and Coffee Counties.

facts.text: The Nation presents its language page as a small learning resource for Tribal members and other Mvskokes.
Its introduction locates the Nation near Troy in Alabama.

nations.name: Delaware Tribe of Indians
nations.lands: Bartlesville, Oklahoma, United States; homelands along the Delaware River

facts.text: The Delaware Tribe of Indians is a federally recognized tribe of the Lenape people, headquartered in Bartlesville, Oklahoma.
The Tribe's online Lenape Talking Dictionary holds about 15,380 words, along with recorded stories and songs, and is still growing.

source.title: Language Revitalization - Delaware Tribe of Indians

pronounce.publisher: Delaware Tribe of Indians, on its own site

nations.name: Sappony
nations.lands: the High Plains Indian Settlement along the North Carolina-Virginia boundary, including Person County, North Carolina, and Halifax County, Virginia, as described by Sappony

facts.text: Sappony describes committees addressing education, cultural preservation and economic development.
Sappony's governance page describes a council with one elected representative from each of the settlement's seven families.

nations.name: The Chickasaw Nation
nations.lands: Thirteen counties in south-central Oklahoma, United States; original homelands in present-day Mississippi, Alabama and Tennessee

facts.text: The Chickasaw Nation's three-department government was reestablished with the ratification of its 1983 Constitution.
The Chickasaw language revitalization program began in 2007, and its master-apprentice program pairs learners with fluent Chickasaw speakers.

nations.name: Catawba Nation
nations.lands: York County, South Carolina, near Rock Hill, with a service area that includes North Carolina, United States

facts.text: After a 20-year effort, a land claim settlement on November 20, 1993 brought the Catawba Indian Nation federal recognition.
The Catawba Nation has over 3,300 enrolled citizens and continues to grow.

nations.name: Haliwa-Saponi Indian Tribe
nations.lands: the Meadows area at present-day Hollister, North Carolina; the Tribe locates its government there without defining territorial boundaries in this source

facts.text: The Tribe describes Red Earth as a program for all ages to learn about Haliwa-Saponi history and cultural practices.

source.title: Cultural Classes - Haliwa Saponi Tribe Resources

facts.text: The Tribal School's stated mission combines academics, technology and community involvement with American Indian culture.

source.title: Haliwa Saponi Tribal School: Quality Education - Haliwa Saponi Tribe Resources

nations.name: Waccamaw Siouan Tribe
nations.lands: Bladen and Columbus Counties in southeastern North Carolina, near Green Swamp

facts.text: Its government page describes a Tribal Council elected by the membership and an Elders Review Committee.
The Tribe's introduction places its communities mainly in Bladen and Columbus Counties, North Carolina, near Green Swamp.

nations.name: Onondaga Nation
nations.lands: Onondaga Nation territory south of Syracuse, central New York, United States

facts.text: In the Haudenosaunee Grand Council, the Onondaga Fire Keepers present an issue, and debate goes on until they can announce that all are of One Mind, a decision by consensus.
The Onondaga Nation is still governed by its traditional government, with fourteen Chiefs and their Clan Mothers serving as caretakers of the land.

nations.name: Cayuga Nation
nations.lands: Around Cayuga Lake in the Finger Lakes region of New York, United States

facts.text: After more than 200 years away, Cayuga Nation citizens once again live on their ancestral homeland in New York's Finger Lakes region.
Every citizen of the Cayuga Nation belongs to one of the Nation's five clans.

nations.name: Pamunkey Indian Tribe
nations.lands: Pamunkey Reservation on the Pamunkey River, King William County, Virginia, United States

facts.text: The U.S. Department of the Interior acknowledged the Pamunkey Indian Tribe as federally recognized, effective January 28, 2016.
The Pamunkey reservation sits on the northern bank of the Pamunkey River in King William County, Virginia.

nations.name: Cherokee Tribe of Northeast Alabama
nations.lands: Northeast Alabama; its own introduction traces its roots to the lower Cherokee towns.

facts.text: Its government page describes a Tribal Council with one representative for each district.
Its Learning Tools page presents a syllabary song and a public word-learning list.

nations.name: Upper Mattaponi Tribe
nations.lands: King William County, Virginia; the Tribe describes its community base as within the traditional lands of Tsenacomacah

facts.text: The Tribe's school history says King William County returned Sharon Indian School to the Tribe in 1987.

source.title: Sharon Indian School Foundation - Upper Mattaponi Tribe

facts.text: The Tribe's history says the Adamstown band became officially known as the Upper Mattaponi Tribe in 1921.

nations.name: Benet
nations.lands: the slopes of Mount Elgon in eastern Uganda, in Kween, Kapchorwa and Bukwo districts

facts.text: In May 2023 Uganda's Office of the Prime Minister directed the wildlife authority (UWA) to stop evictions of Benet communities.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2024, Uganda chapter (IWGIA yearbook PDF)
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: In 2005 Uganda's High Court recognized the Benet as the historical, indigenous inhabitants of Mount Elgon, a landmark land-rights ruling.

source.title: Momentous Ruling Recognizes Land Rights of Indigenous Community

nations.name: Bagyeli
nations.lands: the forests of southern Cameroon, around Akom II, Bipindi, Kribi and Lolodorf

facts.text: In late 2018 Bagyeli communities filed three Community Forest applications with Cameroon's forestry ministry, after mapping their own forest use.

source.title: Secure land tenure: The legal battles of the Bagyeli

facts.text: Bagyeli and Bakola communities live across about 12,000 km2 of southern Cameroon, especially around Akom II, Bipindi, Kribi and Lolodorf.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2024, Cameroon chapter (IWGIA yearbook PDF)
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

nations.name: Ovahimba
nations.lands: Kunene Region of north-western Namibia and south-western Angola

facts.text: Ovahimba speak a Herero language and keep semi-nomadic herding homelands that reach from north-western Namibia into south-western Angola.
Ovahimba are mainly herders whose homes lie in the dry mountains and plains of north-west Namibia's Kunene Region.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2026: Namibia
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

nations.name: Oromo
nations.lands: Oromia and other regions of Ethiopia, and northern Kenya

facts.text: Knowledge of the Gada system is passed on to Oromo children today, at home and at school.

source.title: Gada system, an indigenous democratic socio-political system of the Oromo

facts.text: UNESCO lists the Gada system as an indigenous democratic socio-political system of the Oromo, inscribed on its heritage list in 2016.

source.title: Gada system, an indigenous democratic socio-political system of the Oromo

nations.name: Ishelhiyen
nations.lands: the Souss valley, the Anti-Atlas and the western High Atlas of south-western Morocco

facts.text: In the Souss-Massa region, 63.2% of residents use Tachelhit, the language of the Ishelhin, according to Morocco's 2024 census.

source.title: RGPH 2024: Caractéristiques démographiques et socioéconomiques de la population, Région Souss-Massa
source.publisher: Haut-Commissariat au Plan (HCP), Direction Régionale de Souss Massa

facts.text: Tachelhit, the language of the Ishelhin of southern Morocco, is one of three Amazigh languages taught at Inalco in Paris.

source.title: Kabyle (Berber)
source.publisher: Inalco (Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales)

nations.name: Hadzabe
nations.lands: the hills and valleys around Lake Eyasi in northern Tanzania

facts.text: Hadzabe communities are calling for community-led tourism that ensures transparency, dignity and a fair share of the benefits.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2026: Tanzania
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: Hadza people speak Hadzane, a language isolate, which means it is not related to any other known language.

nations.name: Nama
nations.lands: southern Namibia and the Richtersveld and Namaqualand areas of South Africa's Northern Cape, with smaller communities in Botswana

facts.text: In 2003 South Africa's Constitutional Court recognized the Richtersveld Nama community's communal Indigenous right to its land and the resources in it.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2026: South Africa
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: In South Africa's Richtersveld, Nama families still build portable rush-mat houses called haru oms and move herds between seasonal grazing grounds.

nations.name: Mbororo
nations.lands: Cameroon, Chad, Nigeria, the Central African Republic and Niger, often along borderland grazing routes

facts.text: Hindou Oumarou Ibrahim, a Mbororo woman from Chad who founded the group AFPAT, chaired the UN Permanent Forum on Indigenous Issues for its 2024 session.

source.title: Previous Chairpersons of the Permanent Forum
source.publisher: United Nations, Department of Economic and Social Affairs (UNPFII)

facts.text: Mbororo pastoralists in Cameroon are estimated at over one million people, living mainly near the borders with Nigeria, Chad and the Central African Republic.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2026: Cameroon
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

nations.name: Naro
nations.lands: Ghanzi District in western Botswana, and eastern Namibia

facts.text: In 2025 Botswana's government started radio programs in a number of Indigenous languages, Naro among them.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2026: Botswana
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: Botswana chose Naro, the main San language of Ghanzi District, as one of the mother-tongue languages for primary school teaching from 2022.

source.title: Forty years of fighting for literacy The case of Naro Bible translators

nations.name: Tshwa
nations.lands: Tsholotsho and Bulilimamangwe districts of western Zimbabwe

facts.text: Zimbabwe's 2013 Constitution lists Koisan among its 16 languages, and in 2023 the Tsoro-o-tso San Development Trust worked on the Tjwao language.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2024, Zimbabwe chapter (IWGIA yearbook PDF)
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: About 3,207 Tshwa live in Zimbabwe, where they self-identify as an Indigenous people, mostly in the western districts.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2024, Zimbabwe chapter (IWGIA yearbook PDF)
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

nations.name: Batwa
nations.lands: south-western Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi and the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo

facts.text: In Burundi, Batwa have been represented in the country's main decision-making bodies since 2005.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2023: Burundi
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: In 2021 Uganda's Constitutional Court found that Batwa were evicted from ancestral lands without consent and sent the question of compensation to a lower court.

source.title: MRG welcomes Uganda court verdict on Batwa compensation

nations.name: Samburu
nations.lands: Samburu County and nearby rangelands of north-central Kenya

facts.text: All of Reteti's elephant keepers come from the Samburu community and are formally trained to care for, rehabilitate and release elephant calves.

source.title: Home | Reteti Elephant Sanctuary in Kenya

facts.text: With support from the Samburu Women's Trust, Samburu women are exercising land rights: 20 women and three women's groups own land in one home area.

source.title: Empowering women means taking a stand for environmental rights

nations.name: Khoikhoi
nations.lands: South Africa, especially the Western, Northern and Eastern Cape, including Nama, Griqua and Korana communities

facts.text: Rooibos benefit money now helps fund local schools, water pumps, student fees and an organic rooibos nursery in Cederberg communities such as Wupperthal.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2026: South Africa
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: The Khoisan revival is an ongoing cultural, social and academic movement in South Africa, centred on identity and reclaiming history.

source.title: Kora: A Lost Khoisan Language of the early Cape and the Gariep, Introduction (Menán du Plessis)

nations.name: ǂKhomani
nations.lands: the southern Kalahari in South Africa's Northern Cape, including the Kalahari Gemsbok National Park near the borders with Botswana and Namibia

facts.text: ǂKhomani people have won back cultural rights in South Africa's Kalahari Gemsbok National Park, such as using its resources and hunting in traditional ways across much of it.
The ǂKhomani are actively reclaiming their knowledge and traditions. Their Kalahari homeland became a UNESCO World Heritage cultural landscape in 2017.

nations.name: Ju|'hoansi
nations.lands: Nyae Nyae and the Tsumkwe area of north-eastern Namibia, and neighbouring north-western Botswana

facts.text: When Ju|'hoansi formed their farmers' cooperative, they began with open consensus meetings, then elected two representatives per community, at least one of them a woman.

source.title: Controlling Their Destiny: Ju|'hoansi of Nyae Nyae

facts.text: Ju|'hoansi is the one San language Namibia has approved for teaching in schools, but a 2025 review of 14 schools found it is seldom used in class.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2026: Namibia
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

nations.name: Mbuti
nations.lands: the Ituri forest of north-eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo

facts.text: A 2022 national law in the DR Congo, in force since February 2023, recognizes the rights of Indigenous peoples, including the Mbuti, to their lands, territories and resources.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2024: Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC)
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: UNESCO calls for ensuring the involvement of the Indigenous Mbuti and Efe peoples in the management of the Okapi Wildlife Reserve.

nations.name: Karimojong
nations.lands: the Karamoja drylands of north-eastern Uganda

facts.text: The Karimojong, whose economy has long rested on livestock, live mainly in the drylands of north-eastern Uganda, about 1.09 million people in a 2018 estimate.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2024, Uganda chapter (IWGIA yearbook PDF)
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: Cultural Heritage Clubs in five secondary schools in Napak and Moroto treat heritage as central to Karimojong history and identity.

source.title: Karamoja Cultural Heritage Education Programme
source.publisher: Kara-Tunga (partner of Cross Cultural Foundation Uganda)

nations.name: !Xun
nations.lands: north-eastern Namibia and southern Angola, and Platfontein near Kimberley in South Africa

facts.text: In South Africa, !Xun and Khwe communities live mainly at Platfontein, near Kimberley.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2024, South Africa chapter (IWGIA yearbook PDF)
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: XK FM, a public station first on air in 2000, now broadcasts from Platfontein about 15 hours a day in the !Xun and Khwe languages.

source.title: MEDIA STATEMENT | SABC CELEBRATES THE HISTORY AND CULTURE OF THE !XU AND KHWE

nations.name: Maasai
nations.lands: southern Kenya and northern Tanzania, on both sides of the border

facts.text: In 2025 Tanzania's Simanjiro district paused carbon project signings for 30 days to respond to community concerns, which IWGIA read as a sign that communities are starting to be heard.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2026: Tanzania
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: Maasai people speak Maa, a Nilotic language related to Dinka, Kalenjin and Nuer.

nations.name: Korana
nations.lands: Kimberley and the Free State province, South Africa

facts.text: Korana communities live mainly in Kimberley and in the Free State province.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2024, South Africa chapter (IWGIA yearbook PDF)
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: In their own !Ora language, the Korana's name for themselves is !Orakua or !Orana.

source.title: Kora: A Lost Khoisan Language of the early Cape and the Gariep, Introduction (Menán du Plessis)

nations.name: Afar
nations.lands: the Afar region of north-eastern Ethiopia, the Dankalia coast of Eritrea, and Djibouti

facts.text: In 2008 Afar pastoralists set up the Afar Pastoralist Council so they could raise their voices at regional, national and international level.

source.title: Afar Pastoralist Council holds Inaugural General Meeting

facts.text: Ethiopia's Afar State is home to about 1.8 million Afar people, by a government projection.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2024, Eritrea chapter (IWGIA yearbook PDF)
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

nations.name: Osage Nation
nations.lands: Osage Nation Reservation, northeastern Oklahoma, United States; headquarters in Pawhuska

facts.text: The Osage Minerals Council, an elected body of eight members, is part of the Osage Nation's government.
Since 2006 the Osage Nation has governed itself under a constitution with separate executive, legislative and judicial branches.

nations.name: Standing Rock Sioux Tribe
nations.lands: Standing Rock Reservation, across North Dakota and South Dakota, United States

facts.text: Today Yanktonai Dakota communities live mostly on the North Dakota side of Standing Rock, and Lakota communities mostly on the South Dakota side.
The Standing Rock Tribal Council has a Chairman, Vice-Chairman, Secretary and 14 council members, all elected by tribal members for four-year terms.

source.title: Standing Rock Sioux Tribe | Indian Affairs Commission, North Dakota

nations.name: Pawnee Nation of Oklahoma
nations.lands: Pawnee, Oklahoma, United States; ancestral homeland on the central Plains

facts.text: The Pawnee Business Council is the supreme governing body of the Pawnee Nation, acting within the nation's Constitution and federal law.
The Pawnee Nation is made up of four bands: the Čawî’ (Grand), Kitkahaki (Republican), Pitahawirata (Tappage) and Skidi (Wolf).

source.title: Pawnee History | Pawnee Nation of Oklahoma

nations.name: Ponca Tribe of Nebraska
nations.lands: Fifteen-county service area across Nebraska, Iowa and South Dakota, United States

facts.text: The tribe serves its people across a fifteen-county service area in Nebraska, Iowa and South Dakota, set up by the Ponca Restoration Act.
The Ponca Restoration Act, signed by President George H. W. Bush, restored federal recognition to the Ponca Tribe of Nebraska.

nations.name: Cheyenne River Sioux Tribe
nations.lands: Cheyenne River Reservation, central South Dakota, United States; headquarters in Eagle Butte

facts.text: The tribe is governed by a Chairman, Vice-Chairman, Secretary, Treasurer and fifteen council members, with headquarters in Eagle Butte.

source.title: Cheyenne River Agency | Indian Affairs
source.publisher: U.S. Department of the Interior, Bureau of Indian Affairs

facts.text: The Cheyenne River Reservation holds about 1.45 million trust acres in Ziebach and Dewey counties in central South Dakota.

source.title: Cheyenne River Agency | Indian Affairs
source.publisher: U.S. Department of the Interior, Bureau of Indian Affairs

nations.name: Iowa Tribe of Kansas and Nebraska
nations.lands: Reservation along the Kansas and Nebraska border, United States

facts.text: The tribe is governed by two bodies, a General Council and an Executive Committee.

source.title: Welcome to the Iowa Tribe of Kansas and Nebraska
source.publisher: Iowa Tribe of Kansas and Nebraska

facts.text: The reservation of the Iowa Tribe of Kansas and Nebraska straddles the eastern border between the two states, and tribal headquarters is on it.

source.title: Welcome to the Iowa Tribe of Kansas and Nebraska
source.publisher: Iowa Tribe of Kansas and Nebraska

nations.name: Mandan, Hidatsa, and Arikara Nation
nations.lands: Fort Berthold Indian Reservation, central North Dakota, United States

facts.text: The MHA Nation is governed by a Chairman and six Segment Representatives, one each for White Shield, Parshall, New Town, Four Bears, Mandaree and Twin Buttes.

source.title: MHA Nation | Mandan, Hidatsa, and Arikara Nation

facts.text: The nation greets visitors in all three of its languages. In Mandan, Ráátinitak shí’sh means it is good that you all arrived.

source.title: MHA Nation | Mandan, Hidatsa, and Arikara Nation

nations.name: Northern Arapaho Tribe
nations.lands: Wind River Reservation, Wyoming, United States, shared with the Eastern Shoshone

facts.text: The Northern Arapaho and the Eastern Shoshone share a 2.2 million acre reservation in Wyoming, between the Wind River Range and the Owl Creek Mountains.
The Arapaho Flag was created in 1936 to honor and remember Arapaho war veterans.

nations.name: Sac and Fox Nation
nations.lands: Central Oklahoma, United States; headquarters in Stroud

facts.text: The Sac and Fox Nation supports learning Sauk through an interactive language website and a concise Sauk dictionary.
The Sac and Fox Nation was the first tribe to take on self-governance within the Indian Health Service.

nations.name: Forest County Potawatomi
nations.lands: Forest County, northern Wisconsin, United States

facts.text: The Forest County Potawatomi Language and Culture Department works to keep the Bodwéwadmi language and traditions alive, with classes during the school year.
The Forest County Potawatomi Cultural Center, Library and Museum provides an important link to the community's past.

nations.name: Red Lake Nation
also: Red Lake Band of Chippewa Indians
nations.lands: Red Lake Reservation, northern Minnesota, United States

facts.text: The Red Lake tribal government holds full sovereignty over its reservation, subject only to the federal government.

source.title: Red Lake Nation - Home of the Red Lake Band of Chippewa Indians

facts.text: English is a second language for many Red Lake members who are middle-aged and older, including some on the Tribal Council, and many others speak or understand Ojibwe.

nations.name: Kiowa Tribe
nations.lands: Southwestern Oklahoma, United States

facts.text: The Kiowa Tribe commits to protecting its sovereignty and to preserving and advocating for Kiowa culture and language.

source.title: Kiowa Tribe - Tribe, Native American, Native, Tribe

facts.text: The Kiowa Language Department runs a credentialed teacher training program to prepare new Kiowa language teachers.

pronounce.text: Gáuigú, as in Gáuigú bà dàu, We are Kiowa: Gkawy-goo
pronounce.publisher: Kiowa Tribe, on its own site

nations.name: Blackfeet Nation
nations.lands: Blackfeet Reservation, northwestern Montana, bordering Canada and Glacier National Park, United States

facts.text: The Blackfeet Reservation covers about one and a half million acres, bordered by Canada to the north and Glacier National Park to the west.

source.title: Blackfeet Nation
source.publisher: Montana Governor's Office of Indian Affairs

facts.text: The Blackfeet Nation describes itself as a nation of 17,321 members.

nations.name: Little Traverse Bay Bands of Odawa Indians
nations.lands: Northern Lower Peninsula of Michigan, United States

facts.text: The tribe is governed by a nine-member Tribal Council whose members serve staggered terms.

source.title: Home - LTBB Official Website
source.publisher: Little Traverse Bay Bands of Odawa Indians

facts.text: The tribe's mission celebrates that its people still have and speak their own language, Anishinaabemowin.

source.title: Home - LTBB Official Website
source.publisher: Little Traverse Bay Bands of Odawa Indians

nations.name: Menominee Indian Tribe of Wisconsin
nations.lands: Menominee Reservation, northeastern Wisconsin, United States

facts.text: The Menominee Tribal Legislature has nine members.
The Menominee Reservation covers about 235,524 acres in Wisconsin and holds the largest single tract of virgin timberland in the state.

nations.name: Otoe-Missouria Tribe
nations.lands: Red Rock, Oklahoma; historical homelands include Nebraska and the lower Missouri River valley

facts.text: The Tribe's government page describes a seven-member Tribal Council elected by qualified Tribal voters using a secret ballot.
The Tribe's preservation page dates National Park Service recognition of its Tribal Historic Preservation Office to spring 2016.

nations.name: Fort Peck Assiniboine and Sioux Tribes
nations.lands: Fort Peck Reservation, northeastern Montana, United States; headquarters in Poplar

facts.text: Members of the Fort Peck Tribal Executive Board, except the secretary-accountant, are elected at-large every two years.

source.title: Fort Peck Assiniboine and Sioux Tribes
source.publisher: Montana Governor's Office of Indian Affairs

facts.text: The Fort Peck Reservation in northeastern Montana includes more than two million acres of land.

source.title: Fort Peck Assiniboine and Sioux Tribes
source.publisher: Montana Governor's Office of Indian Affairs

nations.name: Prairie Band Potawatomi Nation
nations.lands: Reservation near Mayetta, northeastern Kansas, United States

facts.text: The Nation has offered Potawatomi language classes since 2007 as part of its work to revitalize the language and culture.

source.title: Prairie Band Potawatomi Language Revitalization Efforts

facts.text: The Prairie Band Potawatomi Nation says its Kansas reservation is unchanged from what the Treaty of 1846 established.

source.title: Prairie Band Potawatomi Tribal History: Origins, Separation, and Stewardship

nations.name: Ho-Chunk Nation
nations.lands: Wisconsin, United States, on lands in many places rather than one reservation; traditional lands also reach Minnesota, Iowa, Missouri and Illinois

facts.text: The Ho-Chunk Nation has four branches of government, with a legislature of 13 members elected from four districts.
Alongside its constitutional government, the Ho-Chunk Nation keeps a traditional system of leadership based on chiefs and clans.

nations.name: Sicangu Lakota Oyate
nations.lands: Rosebud Reservation, South Dakota, United States

facts.text: The tribe's history page says the Lakota number about 70,000 today, and that about a third of them still speak their ancestral language.
The Rosebud Reservation takes in 20 communities, and the tribal headquarters is in the community of Rosebud, South Dakota.

nations.name: Muskeg Lake Cree Nation
nations.lands: Treaty 6 territory in central Saskatchewan, Canada, with urban reserve land in Saskatoon

facts.text: Muskeg Lake Cree Nation planned a gathering for August 20 to 23, 2026 to mark 150 years since Treaty 6 was signed.

source.title: Muskeg Lake Cree Nation, Band No. 102

facts.text: In 1988 Muskeg Lake Cree Nation created Asimakeniseekan Askiy in Saskatoon, the first commercial urban reserve in Canada.

nations.name: Gitxsan
nations.lands: The Laxyip along the upper Skeena River and its tributaries in northern British Columbia, Canada

facts.text: Gitxsan society is matriarchal, with four clans made up of independent Houses (Huwilp), each led by a Wii Simoogit, or high chief.
Gitxsanimaax, the traditional Gitxsan language, has two dialects: Giigeenix, spoken up river, and Gyeets, spoken down river.

nations.name: Piikani Nation
nations.lands: Around Brocket in southern Alberta, Canada, near the Old Man River; part of the Blackfoot Confederacy

facts.text: Piikani stories, ceremonies and songs describe an ancestral territory reaching north to the North Saskatchewan River and west into the Rocky Mountains.
Piikani Nation had 3,928 registered members as of September 2026.

source.title: First Nation Profiles: Registered Population (Piikani Nation)
source.publisher: Crown-Indigenous Relations and Northern Affairs Canada

nations.name: Atikamekw
nations.lands: Nitaskinan in central Quebec, Canada, with the communities of Manawan, Wemotaci and Opitciwan

facts.text: The Atikamekw language, like other Algonquin and Anishinaabe languages, is rich in imagery and names things by how they truly are.
Young people aged 0 to 35 make up about 65 percent of the Atikamekw population today.

nations.name: Innu
nations.lands: Nitassinan: Labrador (Newfoundland and Labrador) and eastern Quebec, Canada

facts.text: In 2008 the Innu Nation and Newfoundland and Labrador signed the Tshash Petapen, or New Dawn, Agreement.

source.title: Innu Nation of Labrador
source.publisher: Government of Newfoundland and Labrador, Indigenous Affairs and Reconciliation

facts.text: The Innu Nation land claim, accepted for negotiation in 1978, covers about 70 percent of Labrador.

source.title: Innu Nation of Labrador
source.publisher: Government of Newfoundland and Labrador, Indigenous Affairs and Reconciliation

nations.name: Six Nations of the Grand River
nations.lands: Along the Grand River in southern Ontario, Canada

facts.text: It is the only First Nation community home to all six Haudenosaunee nations: Mohawk, Cayuga, Onondaga, Oneida, Seneca and Tuscarora.

source.title: Who We Are
source.publisher: Six Nations of the Grand River

facts.text: No First Nation in Canada has a larger population than Six Nations of the Grand River.

source.title: Who We Are
source.publisher: Six Nations of the Grand River

nations.name: Haíɫzaqv
nations.lands: The Central Coast of British Columbia, Canada, centred on Bella Bella (Wáglísla) on Campbell Island

facts.text: In 2025 Heiltsuk members ratified a written constitution, a milestone in self-governance.
Haíɫzaqv means 'to speak and act correctly', principles that guide Heiltsuk ancestral and present-day ways of life.

nations.name: Tłı̨chǫ
nations.lands: Between Great Slave Lake and Great Bear Lake in the Northwest Territories, Canada, around the communities of Behchokǫ̀, Whatì, Gamètì and Wekweètì

facts.text: The Tłı̨chǫ Agreement, in effect since August 4, 2005, was the first combined land, resources and self-government agreement in the Northwest Territories.

source.title: Concluding and Implementing Land and Resources and Self-Government Agreements: Tłı̨chǫ
source.publisher: Government of the Northwest Territories, Executive and Indigenous Affairs

facts.text: The Tłı̨chǫ Government makes laws for its citizens in areas including education, child and family services, and Tłı̨chǫ language and culture.

source.title: Concluding and Implementing Land and Resources and Self-Government Agreements: Tłı̨chǫ
source.publisher: Government of the Northwest Territories, Executive and Indigenous Affairs

nations.name: Secwépemc
nations.lands: Secwepemcúl’ecw, a large territory in the interior of British Columbia, Canada, stretching from the Columbia River valley west to the Fraser River

facts.text: The Shuswap Nation Tribal Council brings together nine Secwépemc communities in the Southern Interior of British Columbia.
Secwépemc Chiefs formed the Shuswap Nation Tribal Council in 1980 to advance Aboriginal rights, self-government and the settlement of land title.

nations.name: Inuvialuit
nations.lands: The Inuvialuit Settlement Region in the western Arctic, Northwest Territories and Yukon, Canada

facts.text: Six communities lie within the Inuvialuit Settlement Region: Aklavik, Inuvik, Paulatuk, Sachs Harbour, Tuktoyaktuk and Ulukhaktok.
One of the agreement's basic goals is keeping Inuvialuit cultural identity and values strong as northern society changes.

nations.name: Kainai
nations.lands: Southern Alberta, Canada, with its main community at Standoff; part of the Blackfoot Confederacy

facts.text: The Blood Tribe's stated mission is to preserve and protect its lands, culture, language and traditions in the spirit of Kainayssini.
In 2026 the Blood Tribe Land Management Department won a Prairie Conservation Award.

nations.name: Eeyou
also: Grand Council of the Crees (Eeyou Istchee)
nations.lands: Eeyou Istchee, the lands east of James Bay and Hudson Bay in northern Quebec, Canada

facts.text: Each Eeyou First Nation runs its own local government, and every elected Chief also sits on the board of the Grand Council of the Crees to address shared issues.

source.title: The Eeyou of Eeyou Istchee
source.publisher: Grand Council of the Crees (Eeyou Istchee) / Cree Nation Government

facts.text: Eeyou Istchee is home to more than 20,000 people.

source.title: The Eeyou of Eeyou Istchee
source.publisher: Grand Council of the Crees (Eeyou Istchee) / Cree Nation Government

nations.name: Nation Wendat
nations.lands: Wendake, near Québec City, within the traditional territory Onyionhwentsïio’ in Quebec, Canada

facts.text: After the Wendat language went dormant in the 1800s, the Yawenda project (2007 to 2012) brought language specialists and community members together to revive it.
The Nation counts more than 300 Wendat businesses, including many artisans, artists and cultural organizations.

nations.name: səlilwətaɬ
nations.lands: Burrard Inlet (səlilwət) in North Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada

facts.text: Tsleil-Waututh people see caring for the lands and waters of their territory as a birthright and obligation, so future generations can thrive.
Tsleil-Waututh means 'People of the Inlet'. The Nation's language is hən̓q̓əmin̓əm, in which its name is səlilwətaɬ.

nations.name: Akwesasne
nations.lands: Along the St. Lawrence River where Ontario, Quebec and New York State meet, in Canada and the United States

facts.text: Akwesasne spans lands in Quebec, Ontario and New York State, and three separate but linked political bodies govern it.
Kanien'kéha, the Mohawk language, remains central to identity in Akwesasne and is actively taught in its schools.

nations.name: Sḵwx̱wú7mesh Úxwumixw
nations.lands: The North Shore of Vancouver and the Squamish River valley, British Columbia, Canada

facts.text: The Nation's roots lie in several communities that became one government in 1923. Most members live on Vancouver's North Shore, others along the Squamish River.
The Squamish language is a sign of resilience: dozens of Nation members are learning it from their Elders as a second language.

nations.name: Tsuut’ina Nation
nations.lands: Treaty 7 territory in southern Alberta, Canada, bordering the city of Calgary

facts.text: Tsuut'ina Nation describes itself today as a highly sufficient and economically advanced First Nation.
Tsuut'ina is the only Dene-speaking nation in Treaty 7 territory, linked to the wider Dene Nation by its Athabaskan language.

nations.name: Vuntut Gwitchin First Nation
nations.lands: Old Crow and the surrounding homeland in northern Yukon, Canada

facts.text: Old Crow, a fly-in community of about 300 people on the Porcupine River, is the seat of the Vuntut Gwitchin government.
Dinjii Zhuh k'yuu, the Gwich'in language, is the official language of the Vuntut Gwitchin First Nation, which is training teachers and raising young speakers.

nations.name: Southern Ute Indian Tribe
nations.lands: Southern Ute Reservation around Ignacio, southwestern Colorado, United States

facts.text: The Southern Ute Indian Tribe is made up of the Mouache and Caputa bands and is headquartered in Ignacio, Colorado.
An elected Tribal Council governs the Southern Ute Indian Tribe, which maintains its own constitution, laws and tribal courts.

nations.name: San Carlos Apache
nations.lands: Gila, Graham and Pinal counties, southeastern Arizona, US

facts.text: The San Carlos Apache Reservation, set aside in 1871, covers 1,834,781 acres reaching from alpine meadows to desert in southeastern Arizona.
More than a third of San Carlos land is forest or woodland, giving a home to elk, mule deer, black bear, turkeys and mountain lion.

nations.name: A:shiwi
nations.lands: Pueblo of Zuni along the Zuni River in western New Mexico, US, with reservation land in Arizona

facts.text: The Pueblo of Zuni counts about 18,692 people and holds about 463,287 acres of reservation land.
For about the last 300 years most Zuni people have lived in one main village, the Pueblo of Zuni, with farming villages used at planting and harvest.

nations.name: Lipan Apache Tribe
nations.lands: Texas, United States, with tribal administration in McAllen and historical homelands spanning Texas and northern Mexico

facts.text: The Lipan Apache Tribe in Texas maintains a Tribal Council responsible for community welfare and protection of its heritage.
In 2021, the City and County of Presidio donated a Lipan cemetery parcel to the Lipan Apache Tribe.

source.title: El Cementerio de los Lipanes Transferred to Tribe

nations.name: Ute Indian Tribe
also: Ute Indian Tribe of the Uintah and Ouray Reservation
nations.lands: Uintah and Ouray Reservation, northeastern Utah, with tribal government at Fort Duchesne, United States

facts.text: In an April 2026 statement, the Ute Indian Tribe announced it would appeal a federal district court decision concerning split-estate reservation lands.

source.title: Tribe will appeal Utah Federal District Court decision on split estate lands

facts.text: The Ute Indian Tribe elects Business Committee representatives from the Uintah, Uncompahgre and Whiteriver bands.

nations.name: Taos Pueblo
nations.lands: Taos valley, northern New Mexico, US

facts.text: Tiwa is the native language of Taos Pueblo, and English and Spanish are also spoken there.
In 1970 a federal law returned 48,000 acres, including Blue Lake, to Taos Pueblo, a landmark for tribal self-determination across the United States.

nations.name: Wixárika
nations.lands: Sierra Madre Occidental in Jalisco and Nayarit, Mexico, with communities in Durango and Zacatecas

facts.text: At the end of the 1700s Wixárika communities received land titles that defined the boundaries of their present-day communities.

source.title: Huicholes
source.publisher: Sistema de Información Cultural, Secretaría de Cultura (Mexico)

facts.text: In July 2025 UNESCO added the Wixárika Route through sacred sites to Wirikuta, a 500 km corridor, to the World Heritage List after decades of Wixaritari requests.

source.title: Boletín No. 334: La Ruta Wixárika por los sitios sagrados a Wirikuta es inscrita en la Lista de Patrimonio Mundial de la UNESCO
source.publisher: Instituto Nacional de Antropología e Historia (INAH)

nations.name: Acoma
nations.lands: Acoma Mesa and surrounding lands in west-central New Mexico, US

facts.text: Since 2017 the Acoma Language Program has been building a Keres dictionary, with about 5,000 words and phrases being edited by fluent speakers.
In 1999 Acoma set up a Historic Preservation Office to keep traditional skills alive, among them stone cutting, wood carving, pottery making and weaving.

nations.name: Southern Paiute
nations.lands: Southern Utah and northern Arizona, US, including Cedar City, Utah, and the Kaibab reservation near Fredonia, Arizona

facts.text: The Paiute Indian Tribe of Utah Restoration Act of April 3, 1980 brought formal federal recognition to the Cedar Band of Paiute Indians.
The Paiute Indian Tribe of Utah shares The Paiute Language for Beginners, now in its second edition, which anyone can view and download.

nations.name: Rarámuri
nations.lands: Sierra Tarahumara in Chihuahua, Mexico, with smaller communities in Durango, Sonora and Sinaloa

facts.text: Rarámuri artisans make violins, drums, palm baskets, clay pots and wooden masks, and sell them in towns such as Guachochi, Creel and Batopilas.

source.title: Tarahumaras
source.publisher: Sistema de Información Cultural, Secretaría de Cultura (Mexico)

facts.text: The Rarámuri ball race is a contest in which runners cover long distances while kicking a wooden ball, and it is held as part of community fiestas.

source.title: Tarahumaras
source.publisher: Sistema de Información Cultural, Secretaría de Cultura (Mexico)

nations.name: Tohono O’odham
nations.lands: Sonoran Desert of southern Arizona, US (Sells is the capital), with O’odham communities across the border in Sonora, Mexico

facts.text: Divided by the border since the 1850s, O’odham communities in Sonora, Mexico, and Arizona still share a common culture and sense of being one people.

source.title: Pápagos
source.publisher: Sistema de Información Cultural, Secretaría de Cultura (Mexico)

facts.text: O’odham groups still speak the O’odham language, part of the Uto-Aztecan family, with dialects that vary from group to group.

nations.name: Hopi
nations.lands: Hopitutskwa, northeastern Arizona, US (Navajo and Coconino counties)

facts.text: Hopi government is unicameral. Its powers rest with a Tribal Council of village representatives, who serve two year terms.
The Hopi Reservation in northeastern Arizona covers more than 1.5 million acres and is made up of 12 villages on three mesas.

source.title: The Official Website of the Hopi Tribe

nations.name: Kha’P’o
nations.lands: From the eastern Jemez Mountains to the Rio Grande, northern New Mexico, US

facts.text: People of Santa Clara Pueblo still speak the Tewa language today and carry on their customs and cultural activities.
Santa Clara is one of six Tewa-speaking villages, and its reservation covers about 90 square miles from the Jemez Mountains to the Rio Grande.

nations.name: Kumeyaay
nations.lands: San Diego and Imperial counties, California, US, and Tecate, Ensenada and Rosarito in Baja California, Mexico

facts.text: North of the US and Mexico border there are 12 Kumeyaay Nation bands today, each original to Kumeyaay territory. Sycuan is one of them.

source.title: History & Heritage
source.publisher: Sycuan Band of the Kumeyaay Nation

facts.text: In Baja California the Kumiai call themselves Tipai. Their communities sit on the coastal plateaus of Ensenada and Rosarito and in Tecate.

source.title: Kumiais
source.publisher: Sistema de Información Cultural, Secretaría de Cultura (Mexico)

nations.name: Yoeme
nations.lands: Yaqui River valley in Sonora, Mexico, and Pascua Yaqui communities near Tucson, Arizona, US

facts.text: Most Yoeme people today live in the Mexican states of Sonora and Sinaloa, and the federally recognized Pascua Yaqui Tribe is based in Tucson, Arizona.
The Pascua Yaqui Tribe in Arizona gained United States federal recognition on September 18, 1978.

nations.name: Chiricahua Apache Nation
nations.lands: Headquarters in Santa Clara, New Mexico, United States; this record describes this named community, not every Chiricahua Apache person or government

facts.text: The Chiricahua Apache Nation lists its tribal headquarters in Santa Clara, New Mexico.
Its foundation's stated work includes education, social welfare and defending Chiricahua Apache self-determination.

nations.name: Shipibo-Konibo
nations.lands: Ucayali, Madre de Dios, Loreto and Huánuco in Peru, with an urban community at Cantagallo in Lima

facts.text: Cantagallo, home to Shipibo-Konibo families, is the best known Amazonian Indigenous settlement in metropolitan Lima.

source.title: Shipibo-Konibo | BDPI
source.publisher: Ministerio de Cultura del Perú, Base de Datos de Pueblos Indígenas u Originarios

facts.text: In Peru's 2017 national census, 25,232 people identified as part of the Shipibo-Konibo people.

source.title: Shipibo-Konibo | BDPI
source.publisher: Ministerio de Cultura del Perú, Base de Datos de Pueblos Indígenas u Originarios

nations.name: Tupinambá
nations.lands: Atlantic Forest of southern Bahia around Olivença, in Ilhéus, Buerarema and Una, with Tupinambá communities also in Pará, Brazil

facts.text: The Tupinambá of Olivença live in the Atlantic Forest region of southern Bahia.
In 2001 Funai, Brazil's Indigenous affairs agency, officially recognized the Tupinambá of Olivença as an Indigenous people.

nations.name: Guarani Kaiowá
nations.lands: Southern Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil, and neighboring eastern Paraguay, where the people are known as Paĩ Tavyterã

facts.text: Kaiowá, Ñandeva and Mbya Guarani all speak dialects of Guarani and show strong energy in keeping their language alive.

source.title: Guarani Kaiowá - Povos Indígenas no Brasil

facts.text: Guarani communities today call the places they live tekoha, a word that joins land, forest, fields, water, animals, plants and medicines.

source.title: Guarani Kaiowá - Povos Indígenas no Brasil

nations.name: Mẽbêngôkre
nations.lands: Forests and savannas of southern Pará and northern Mato Grosso, Brazil, along rivers of the Xingu basin such as the Iriri, Bacajá and Fresco

facts.text: The Associação Floresta Protegida, created in 1998 by Mẽbêngôkre leaders, represents about 3,000 people in 31 villages across three Indigenous lands.
The Mẽbêngôkre language belongs to the Jê family of the Macro-Jê language stock.

nations.name: Yanomami
nations.lands: Forests of Amazonas and Roraima states in northern Brazil, continuing across the border into southern Venezuela

facts.text: The Yanomami language family is not linked to any other language stock, and it has six languages and sixteen dialects.

source.title: TI Yanomami
source.publisher: Casa Civil da Presidência da República, Governo do Brasil

facts.text: The Yanomami Indigenous Territory in Brazil, about 9.66 million hectares of tropical forest, was ratified by presidential decree on 25 May 1992.

nations.name: Awajún
nations.lands: Northern Peruvian Amazon in Amazonas, Loreto, San Martín, Cajamarca and Ucayali

facts.text: The Federation of Aguaruna Women of the Upper Marañón (FEMAAM), founded in Imaza in 2002, opened the way for Awajún women's political participation.

source.title: Awajún | BDPI
source.publisher: Ministerio de Cultura del Perú, Base de Datos de Pueblos Indígenas u Originarios

facts.text: The Awajún language belongs to the Jivaroan language family.

source.title: Awajún | BDPI
source.publisher: Ministerio de Cultura del Perú, Base de Datos de Pueblos Indígenas u Originarios

nations.name: Wichí
nations.lands: Gran Chaco of northern Argentina, mainly Salta, Formosa and Chaco provinces, with related communities in southern Bolivia

facts.text: In 2010 Argentina's Chaco province made the Wichí, Qom and Moqoit languages official languages of the province alongside Spanish.

source.title: Argentine: les lois provinciales à portée linguistique
source.publisher: L'aménagement linguistique dans le monde, Université Laval (CEFAN)

nations.name: Pueblo Originario Kichwa de Sarayaku
nations.lands: Middle Bobonaza river basin, Pastaza province, Ecuadorian Amazon

facts.text: About 1,500 Kichwa people of Sarayaku live in seven community centers across roughly 135,000 hectares on the Bobonaza river in Pastaza, Ecuador.
Sarayaku has its own statute on image, communication and digital sovereignty, setting free, prior and informed consent rules for visitors, press and researchers.

source.title: Statute of Governance of Image, Communication, and Digital Sovereignty of the Kichwa Indigenous People of Sarayaku

nations.name: Qom
nations.lands: Gran Chaco of northern Argentina, especially Chaco, Formosa and Santa Fe provinces, plus communities in Buenos Aires and in Paraguay

facts.text: The Qom language is being recovered in universities and in community-run spaces, and children and teenagers are taking it up.

source.title: El wichí y el qom comienzan a ser hablados en la primera infancia y en la adolescencia
source.publisher: Unidiversidad, Universidad Nacional de Cuyo (from Télam)

facts.text: Qom is one of three Indigenous languages that Argentina's Chaco province declared official alongside Spanish in 2010.

source.title: Argentine: les lois provinciales à portée linguistique
source.publisher: L'aménagement linguistique dans le monde, Université Laval (CEFAN)

nations.name: Munduruku
nations.lands: Tapajós river basin in Pará, with communities in Amazonas and Mato Grosso, Brazil

facts.text: Munduruku of the upper Tapajós created the Pusuru Indigenous Association in 1991 as a formal way to organize their communities.
The Munduruku language belongs to its own Munduruku family within the Tupi language stock.

nations.name: Waorani
nations.lands: Orellana, Pastaza and Napo provinces in the Ecuadorian Amazon

facts.text: Waorani territory includes 32 communities in three Amazonian provinces of Ecuador: Orellana, Pastaza and Napo.
The legally recognized Waorani territory is governed by NAWE, the Waorani Nationality of Ecuador, regarded as the highest Waorani territorial authority.

nations.name: Huni Kuin
nations.lands: Rivers of Acre state in western Brazil, such as the Tarauacá, Jordão and Purus, and the Purus and Curanja rivers in Peru

facts.text: Huni kuin, the name the people use for themselves, means true people, or people with known customs.

source.title: Huni Kuin (Kaxinawá) - Povos Indígenas no Brasil

facts.text: MAHKU, the Huni Kuin Artists Movement founded in Acre in 2013, painted a large mural across the facade of the Central Pavilion at the 2024 Venice Biennale.

source.title: Biennale Arte 2024 | MAHKU (Movimento dos Artistas Huni Kuin)

nations.name: Tsimane'
nations.lands: Forests and savannas of the Beni department, Bolivia, mainly along the Maniquí and Apere rivers

facts.text: Tsimane' livelihoods center on small farms of plantains, rice, corn and sweet manioc, along with fishing, hunting and gathering.

source.title: Tsimane fieldsite in Bolivia
source.publisher: Culture and the Mind project, University of Sheffield

facts.text: Almost all Tsimane' speak their own Tsimane' language as their main language.

source.title: Tsimane fieldsite in Bolivia
source.publisher: Culture and the Mind project, University of Sheffield

nations.name: Asháninka
nations.lands: Central Peruvian Amazon in Junín, Ucayali, Pasco, Cusco, Huánuco and Ayacucho

facts.text: In 2017, 73,567 people in Peru said Ashaninka was the language they learned to speak as children.

source.title: Ashaninka | BDPI
source.publisher: Ministerio de Cultura del Perú, Base de Datos de Pueblos Indígenas u Originarios

facts.text: In Peru's 2017 national census, 55,493 people identified as part of the Asháninka people.

source.title: Ashaninka | BDPI
source.publisher: Ministerio de Cultura del Perú, Base de Datos de Pueblos Indígenas u Originarios

nations.name: Puyallup Tribe of Indians
